name: Kang-Petrov Arms KP-10M 'Ten-Mike'
description:
The KP-10M is Kang-Petrov's 10mm Combat Auto variant — same polymer-frame striker-fired architecture as the KP-17 and KP-19 family, but scaled up to handle the significantly more powerful 10mm round. The frame is wider at the grip, the slide is heavier, and the recoil spring assembly is a dual-captive-rod unit that tames the 10mm's substantially sharper impulse. Barrel length is 121mm. The magazine holds 14 rounds of 10mm in a double-stack configuration, and the grip circumference is large enough that smaller-handed operators sometimes struggle with the reach to the trigger — Kang-Petrov offers a narrower grip module as an accessory, but it's rarely seen in the field. The trigger is the same flat-face unit found in the KP-30, tuned for 10mm's heavier primer strike requirement. The dust cover rail is standard, and the pistol ships with a recoil buffer pad in the grip that most experienced users remove because it changes the balance.

The KP-10M occupies an unusual market position — it's priced within reach of serious Tier 1 buyers at Φ580, but the 10mm ammunition runs nearly double the cost of 9mm Standard, which effectively prices the gun out of regular practice for most shelf workers. The people who carry it tend to be security professionals who actually have an ammunition budget, or operators who work in environments where 9mm penetration is considered inadequate — warehouse districts, vehicle interdiction, anyone who might need to punch through light cover. A 10mm Workhorse on a shelf worker's hip is either a statement or a story.

The KP-10M has a reputation for being hard on its shooters and harder on people who get shot with it. The 10mm round out of a 121mm barrel is a legitimate stopper in a way that 9mm standard is not, and the gun's felt recoil is significant enough that operators who run it regularly develop a very specific grip technique — thumbs-forward, locked wrists, weight slightly forward. You can identify a KP-10M regular by the way they stand before they've drawn.
specifications: caliber: 10mm Combat Auto effective_range: 70m rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic magazine_capacity: 14 rounds weight: 0.92 kg
tactical_use: The KP-10M is chosen by operators who anticipate needing to defeat light cover or body armor supplements at pistol ranges. The 10mm round maintains energy at extended pistol distances significantly better than 9mm, making the KP-10M viable in semi-open environments where engagements might stretch to 60-70 meters. The trade-off is capacity, ammunition cost, and shooter fatigue in extended training or sustained operations. Security teams running vehicle patrol or warehouse perimeter work favor it for the ability to engage through vehicle glass and light paneling. It is not a gun for casual carry — it demands respect and practice.
cultural_context: In GLMZ, the KP-10M is read as a declaration of seriousness. It costs more to shoot, kicks harder, and kills more definitively — carrying one says you have thought about what you might need to do and decided to be ready for the worst version. Among shelf cooperative defense groups it is the weapon of the person who has been in something bad before. Among Tier 2 security professionals it is the preferred option for anyone who has actually been in a firefight and didn't want to wonder afterward whether their gun was enough.

operators working industrial or warehouse zones
story_hooks: A KP-10M recovered from a shooting scene has had its barrel replaced with an aftermarket unit in 9x19mm — someone wanted the intimidation factor of the 10M frame on camera footage but didn't want to pay 10mm ammunition prices, and the conversion was done badly enough that it's a wonder it didn't detonate in the shooter's hand.

A Slagworks warehouse district security contractor has put in a bulk order for 40 KP-10Ms and 20,000 rounds of 10mm — three times their normal allocation — and the order was approved without the usual budget review that should have flagged it.
